name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Unpaid Salary and Withholding Relieving Letter after Resignation
case_dossier.summary: The employee resigned on 1 Aug 2024, completed the 60‑day notice, but the employer has not paid the September salary and leave encashment of Rs 1,65,000, delayed the August salary, and is refusing to issue the relieving and experience letters, jeopardising the new job offer.

timeline.event: Joined the IT consultancy as a frontend developer with a salary of Rs 70,000 per month.
Served 60‑day notice period, handed over assets (MacBook, ID card) and received asset clearance certificate.
Salary for August was delayed/not received.
September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (Rs 1,65,000) remains unpaid.
No salary paid; HR cites client payment delays; relieving and experience letters withheld.
New employer threatens to cancel job offer if relieving letter is not provided.

evidence_needed: Salary slips for August and September 2024
Bank statements or UPI/NEFT transaction records showing non‑receipt of salary
Complete email/WhatsApp thread with HR/Finance regarding salary delay and relieving letter request
Copy of the company's policy on notice period salary payment and leave encashment
Written acknowledgment from employer about pending dues (if any)
Any internal communication confirming the withholding of relieving/experience letters
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Key documents like appointment letter and clearance form are present, but lacking direct proof of unpaid salary and communications that show the employer's refusal.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a clear legal right to receive the salary and leave encashment that were due for August and September 2024, and also to get your relieving and experience letters. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employer must pay all wages within two working days after an employee resigns (Section 17(2)). The amount you are owed (Rs 1,65,000) is a wage, so the employer’s delay is a breach of that law. The matter is a civil dispute – it is about unpaid wages and a contract breach, not a criminal offence. Because the employer is also refusing to give you the relieving documents, you can claim those as part of the same wage claim, and the labour authorities can order the employer to issue them.

governing_laws.relevance: Requires the employer to pay all wages within two working days of resignation, dismissal or removal.
Limits any deductions to 50% of wages, ensuring the full amount you are owed cannot be arbitrarily reduced.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Clarifies that non‑payment of salary is a civil matter, not a criminal cheating case.

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Notice (Email / Registered Post)
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (postage or email cost)
action_options.details: Draft a concise notice stating: (a) you resigned on 1 Aug 2024 and completed the 60‑day notice; (b) under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, the employer must pay all pending wages within two working days of resignation; (c) you are owed August salary, September salary and leave encashment totalling Rs 1,65,000; (d) you also require the relieving and experience letters; (e) you demand payment and issuance of the letters within 7 days, failing which you will approach the labour authorities. Attach copies of your appointment letter, resignation acceptance, asset clearance form, and any email proof of the resignation.

action_options.title: File a Grievance on the Labour Department Portal (e‑Daakhil / State Labour Commissioner)
action_options.timeline: Within 30 days of sending the notice
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs; nominal filing fee if any
action_options.details: Register on the e‑Daakhil portal (https://e-daakhil.gov.in) or the respective State Labour Commissioner’s website. Upload the legal notice, supporting documents (appointment letter, resignation email, asset clearance, salary slips if available), and a brief statement of claim. The portal will generate a reference number and forward the complaint to the Labour Commissioner, who will issue a notice to the employer to comply.

action_options.title: Approach the Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal
action_options.timeline: 60‑90 days from filing the grievance, depending on the authority’s schedule
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal court fee (around Rs 500‑1,000 for claims up to Rs 2 Lakhs); possible free legal aid from DLSA
action_options.details: If the employer does not comply with the Labour Commissioner’s order, file a plaint in the District Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal having jurisdiction over the employer’s location. You can represent yourself, but a lawyer can help draft the plaint and argue the case. Attach all evidence, including the employer’s response (or lack thereof). The court can order payment of the pending wages, interest, and direct the employer to issue the relieving and experience letters.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can start the process yourself – sending the notice and filing the online grievance do not require a lawyer. However, filing a petition before the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal usually benefits from legal representation, especially to ensure the claim is framed correctly and to handle any defence the employer raises. If you cannot afford a lawyer, approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid (Helpline 15100).
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, humare HR policies aur internal clearance process ke bina hum koi bhi final settlement ya relieving letter issue nahi kar sakte. Aapka resignation acceptance abhi tak HR ke system mein update nahi hua hai, isliye salary aur encashment hold par hai. Company ke standard operating procedure ke mutabik, aapko sabhi pending project deliverables aur asset return ka clearance form sign karna hoga. Jab tak yeh sab complete nahi hota, hum koi payment ya letter release nahi kar sakte. Aapka complaint bhi samajh rahe hain, lekin humare paas bhi apni internal audit ka schedule hai, jo agle hafte tak poora hoga.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: Aapne specific statutory right (full and final dues) aur deadline (3 din) ka zikr kiya, jo aapke claim ko majboot banata hai.
